about: Baronetti («De' Baronetti»), the boys' game of the Turin rulebook «Primi elementi e regole del giuoco de' tarocchi» (Torino, Soffietti, 1787, pp. 47-53), read on its scan: two players, the whole 78-card pack dealt into four piles each of 10, 10, 10 and 9 cards with only the top card of every pile face up (pp. 48-49); only open cards are played, the next card of the pile a player played from is turned after both have played (pp. 49-50); the trick-taker leads (p. 50); the cards are counted in pairs and 46 points win the hand (pp. 51-52); the Fool is never given up, it is only shown and laid among one's points, and its owner gives one plain card of his choice (pp. 50, 52). The book's own purpose is to teach boys to answer in the suit asked (p. 47). Where the book is silent (what a Fool shown inside a trick does to the trick, the tie at 45½, the order of dealers, the Fool led) nothing is invented: the leaf is a [R] reading or the rule is listed in left_out. The money is the simple stake of p. 21; no match is described, and a match of two games is our decision; the loser of a game deals the next (p. 41, through p. 47). Marks: [D] documented, [R] our reading, [S] sources silent. When the piles run unequal the play simply goes on from the open cards (p. 49); that is the engine's behaviour, not a rule.

nice1930.cite: F. Cason, «Les jeux de cartes à Nice», Armanac Nissart, Nice, 1930, pp. 277-290

piedicavallo2008.cite: Zorio Prachin, Il gioco dei tarocchi in Alta Valle Cervo, Piedicavallo, S.O.M.S. and Pro Loco, 2008

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 47: «suolsi solamente giuocare fra due persone»: Baronetti is played only by two.

direction.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35, 37: «gli altri sempre a destra procedendo»: play passes to the right; with two players the direction changes nothing.

first_dealer.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 16: cards are turned up for each side, «se viene prima da questa parte un Trionfo, mischierò io»: the side that first receives a trionfo shuffles and deals first.

cut_by.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 48: «tu coppi il mazzo»: the dealer's opponent cuts and, as the same sentence says, receives «l'avvantaggio della mano», the first lead.

cut_min.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 16: «Una carta sola non si può coppare»: the page forbids only a cut of one card; that each part keeps at least two cards is our reading.

dealer_rotation.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 41 (said in Sedici, the game for two): «rimetterai le carte tutte in mazzo al tuo compagno, il quale dovrà mischiare, e dare»: the winner hands the pack to his companion, so the loser deals; p. 53 sends the rest of Baronetti to the general rules («Le altre regole si potranno riferire ai numeri antecedenti»). Other reading (the value of revisions 9 and 10): the deal alternates, as p. 42 (rule 44) allows that the one who shuffles is the winner («colui, cui tocca a mischiar le carte, è quegli per avventura, che abbia guadagnato») and p. 70, after a drawn hand of Permesso for three, says «tocca al compagno appresso a mischiare»; with two players the alternation and a deal to the right are the same.

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 47, 51: two persons, each counts his own points and «convien poter contare quarantasei punti» to win the hand.

deck.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 48: «Essendo tutti i Tarocchi in numero di settant'otto»: the whole pack is dealt into the eight piles (see also pp. 9-10).

trump_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 13: «l'Angelo, il quale è il XX., appresso noi prende il Mondo»: the trionfi rank by their printed numbers, with the Angel XX above the World XXI («l'usanza, che in questo caso fa legge»); the Fool stands outside the order.

suit_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 11-13: in swords and batons the larger number takes the smaller; in cups and coins «la carta di numero inferiore prende quella di numero superiore, eccetto le figure» (the ace takes the two up to the ten); the courts stand above every numeral. The order among the courts is printed, pp. 11-12: «il Re bensì prende la Donna, il Cavallo, il Fante».

card_points.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 13-14: «Ogni Re conta cinque punti. Ogni Donna conta quattro punti»: king 5, queen 4, knight 3, jack 2, the Angel 5, Bagatto 5, the Fool 5; the World and the other cards carry no value of their own. Values are the book's numbers (a king with a plain card is 5, p. 52). Baronetti repeats the five points of Bagatto and of the Fool on p. 47, and p. 51 counts them in pairs: «con l'Angelo, con Bagatto, col Folle, affinchè veramente conti per cinque punti».

fool.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 47, 50: «nè Bagatto può prendere il Folle, nè il Folle può prendere Bagatto» and «non sarò io obbligato a dartelo mai, ma solo mi basterà mostrarlo»: the Fool takes nothing and is not taken, it is shown and laid among the owner's points.

fool_exchange.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 52: «Chi avrà avuto il Folle, e l'avrà … di dare al compagno una cartaccia».

fool_exchange_card.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 52: «una cartaccia, qualunque gli piaccia»: the owner chooses the plain card he gives, the other has no right to say «Voglio quella». [S] The book is silent on an owner who has no plain card but has other cards (p. 52): the engine offers him the cheapest cards he holds (count.js, plainOptions); that is our decision, not the book's.

fool_exchange_to.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 52: the card is given «al compagno», in this game the opponent. The trick-taker wording belongs to pp. 77-78 (Permesso for five to seven), not to Baronetti.

fool_last_trick.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 50: «non sarò io obbligato a dartelo mai»: the Fool is never lost; the book makes no exception for the last trick.

fool_show_any_time.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 50, 52, 54: showing the Fool answers another's lead in place of a card: p. 54, «solamente si mostra, come nel giuoco de' Baronetti»; the Fool stays with its owner, who gives one plain card of his choice for it (p. 52). What becomes of the trick the book does not say outright (p. 50: «e tu seguiterai a giuocare»); read: the Fool is the owner's card of that trick and takes nothing. Other reading (stood until revision 8): on his own turn the owner of an open Fool may show it and lay it among his won cards without playing it to a trick.

fool_no_tricks.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 50 (Baronetti): «non sarò io obbligato a dartelo mai, ma solo mi basterà mostrarlo» … «e poi metterlo ne' miei punti»: the Fool is never given up, it is shown and laid among the owner's points. Torino 1787, p. 21, rule 10, lists among the things to be agreed before the deal whether a player «avendo o il Folle, o lo scarto» loses the «vola»: it supposes that a player with no trick may hold the Fool, so the Fool stays with him. Our reading: «mai» is said of the play, but by its letter it covers every case, so a player with no trick keeps the Fool; an owner without a plain card gives nothing. Other reading (alt give_fool): Prammatica [1846], p. 6: «chi non potesse coprirlo, alla fine della mano è obbligato di cederlo alla parte vincente»; Torino 1880, p. 9 says only that the Fool of a side with no trick may be taken («as peul piesse»); Dummett 1980, p. 259: «if they have won no tricks, they must surrender the Folle». See OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, question 2.

replace.what: the Fool of a player who won no trick: kept or given up

options.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 21 (rule 10): «quanto si giuochi la partita semplice, qualunque sia il giuoco, che facciasi»: the stake of the simple game is settled before the deal. The book names no amount (p. 15 plays «un quattrino per ciascuna partita» as an example); the list of choices is the table's.

piles.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 48-49: ten cards face down «principiando dalla prima carta, che sta sopra il mazzo», then two more piles of ten, and the last eighteen cards as two piles of nine: «ne do solo nove a te, e l'ultime nove le prendo per me». Each player has four piles, 10, 10, 10, 9. The book has no hand outside the piles.

pile_top.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 48-49: «scoprendoti solo quella, che ultima del mucchietto ti diedi»; the last card of the last pile is turned for both («voltando l'ultima sempre ad ambidue»).

order.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 48: the dealer lays the first pile in front of his opponent, then takes one for himself: «Altrettante carte ... prendo io per me», and so on pile by pile.

face.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 48: «dieci carte coperte»: all cards of a pile lie face down but the top one.

dead.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 48-49: 3 x 10 + 9 for each player is 39 and 39, the whole pack of 78 (the sum is ours); nothing is left over.

first_leader.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 48: «ti do l'avvantaggio della mano»: the dealer's opponent leads the first trick.

next_leader.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 50: «Chi prende giuoca sempre il primiero»: the taker leads, «un grande avvantaggio».

play_from.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 49: «tu giuochi quella carta scoperta, che a te pare e piace»: only open cards are played; the covered cards may not even be looked at (p. 52).

follow_suit.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 49: «ti rispondo senza mai rinegare con una carta della medesima sequenza». [R] The duty is kept to the open cards, since covered cards may not be looked at (p. 52).

must_trump.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 49: «se non ho carte della medesima sequenza prendo con Trionfi»; with no trump the card is thrown away.

must_overtrump.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 49: «Se tu giuochi Trionfo, io rispondo Trionfo, … il Trionfo maggiore, prende la mano»: a trump is answered by a trump and the higher takes; the book states no duty to beat it.

fool_may_lead.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 50 shows the Fool «quando mi vada in acconcio»; ours: it may be led, as in Venticinque. Nice 1930, p. 279 and Piedicavallo 2008, p. 13 let the Fool go «in qualsiasi momento», of other games; neither names the first lead.

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 50: «tutti due volgeremo subito la nostra carta coperta una sola per volta».

reveal.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 50: the covered card is turned «non prima di aver giuocato, e risposto»: after both cards of the trick are played, one card each, at once. [R] That it is the next card of the pile just played from is our reading; the book says «la nostra carta coperta».

empty_pile.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 49-50: not addressed; since only open cards may be played (p. 49), a player whose pile is used up can play only from his other piles.

group.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 51-52: «ogni carta dee essere accompagnata con un'altra carta»; not «una carta sola per volta» as at Sedici and Trent'uno.

count_unit.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 52: a king with a plain card is worth 5, a queen 4, a knight 3, a jack 2, two plain cards 1: a card is worth its points less a half, a plain card a half.

odd_card.source: [R] Torino 1787: an unpaired card at the end is not addressed in Baronetti; read after Venticinque, whose count is «come al giuoco de' Baronetti» (p. 56) and where «Una carta sola, ancorchè scompagnata» counts (pp. 54-55). Other reading: the odd card is dropped.

trick_multipliers.source: [R] Torino 1787: the count is the one the section names; the book prints no trick multiplier and no war in these games (x2 and x4 are Duello's own).

last_trick_bonus.source: [R] Torino 1787: the book prints no bonus for the last trick (the +5 is Duello's own).

winner.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 51: «Per guadagnare la partita convien poter contare quarantasei punti».

target.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 51: «quarantasei punti»; 46 is a majority of the 91 points of the pack counted in pairs (the 91 is not printed).

game_points.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 51, 53: the hand is paid as a stake («pagare la partita»), the book names no game points; settle holds the payment.

tie.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 51-52: 45½ each is not mentioned; ours as Venticinque, p. 54: «faremo eguali». In the main count it cannot happen: both piles stay even, the points are whole and sum to 91.

unit.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 21, 53: the simple game is paid in the stake agreed before the deal; «Le altre regole si potranno riferire ai numeri antecedenti».

mode.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 51: «la partita» is paid by the loser; with two players there is no other reading.

amount.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 21: «quanto si giuochi la partita semplice, qualunque sia il giuoco, che facciasi».

kind.source: [S] Ours: the book describes a hand («la partita»), not a match; the stakes are settled after every game, the match ends after one round of dealers (match.dealer_rounds); the greatest balance wins, equal balances are a draw («pace»).

dealer_rounds.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 47-53 are silent on the length of a match: they end with «Le altre regole si potranno riferire ai numeri antecedenti» (p. 53), and the general rules name none. Ours: one round of dealers, that is two games (the match ends after rounds x seats games); since the loser deals the next game (seats.dealer_rotation, Torino 1787, p. 41), one player may deal both games of a round. The table may agree on two or three rounds.

effect.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 33-34 (rule 35): «pagare a tutti i compagni la partita semplice»; while the cards of the trick are still on the table the card is changed, once the trick is turned and put among the points there is «non vi sarà più remissione».

[D] Torino 1787, pp. 50-51: «Chi volterà due carte per volta, primieramente sarà avvisato di non più farlo»; the second time he pays the game «e se anche la guadagna, non potrà più esigere il suo guadagno». The engine turns the cards itself.
[D] Torino 1787, pp. 52-53: looking at a covered card, the opponent's or one's own, «pagherà la partita doppia, eccetto che ... inavvertentemente», then «la pagherà semplice».
[D] Torino 1787, p. 53: the piles must be dealt «di seguito, e non una per ciascuno alternativamente»; «Chi farà diverso, pagherà la partita secondo l'accordo».

play.value: keep the four piles level and keep all four as long as possible
play.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 51: «Regola è sempre di tenere i mucchietti eguali»: advice of the book; it never binds a human player.

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 47: «Del rimanente osservansi tutte le regole generali dette di sopra»: the general penalties apply, among them a wrong number of cards dealt (pp. 18-19, rule 5: «Pagherai similmente la partita, se darai giuoco fallo»).
left_out.why: The engine deals the piles itself, so a pile with a wrong number of cards cannot happen; nor can the other general offences of the deal and the cut. Only the revoke and the penalties of Baronetti's own pages are listed.
